description: BackgroundTisdale risk score has been validated for predicting drug-induced QTc prolongation (QTP) in cardiac care. This study aims to determine whether it can guide prescribing and monitoring of QTc-prolonging medications in primary care.MethodsA retrospective chart audit using Tisdale Risk Score was conducted.

title: Electrical coupling between transplanted cardiomyocytes and host myocardium to prevent arrhythmia
creator: Bijay Guragain, Lei Ye, Jack M Rogers, Jianyi (Jay) Zhang
description: Transplantation of human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes offers new opportunities for myocardial repair after infarction. However, as demonstrated in large-animal model studies, such therapy also brings translational challenges, including arrhythmias arising from abnormal spontaneous beating of the engrafted cells or irregular conduction due to poor electrical coupling between host and transplanted tissue.

title: Gut microbiota in a Saudi population with chronic kidney disease
creator: Afnan A Almuhanna, Chittibabu Vatte, Qian Guo, Tamer S Elsalamouni, Fahd A Al-Muhanna, Ameen M Aboalrihy, Hassan A Alhabib, Mohammed F Almomen, Rudaynah A Alali, Alawi H Habara, Mohammed A Alrubaish, Kaltham M Alfalah, Cyril Cyrus, Ibrahiem Saeed Abdul-Rahman, Brendan J Keating, Amein K Al-Ali, Chan
description: BACKGROUNDThe gut microbiota (GM) plays an important role in chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, and dialysis modalities can differentially impact the GM composition and function. There is also limited information on the GM in Arab populations.AIMTo investigate the distinct microbial profiles and functional alterations associated with hemodialysis (HD) and peritoneal dialysis (PD) in a Saudi Arabian cohort.

title: Multicentre comparative study of neural epidermal growth factor-like 1 protein vs M-type phospholipase A2 receptor-associated membranous nephropathy
creator: Subrahmanian Sathiavageesan, Abirami Krishnan, Krishnaswamy Sampathkumar, Ranjanee Muthu
description: BACKGROUNDThe understanding of membranous nephropathy (MN) has significantly evolved with the discovery of novel antigenic targets. M-type phospholipase A2 receptor-associated MN (PLA2R-MN) is the most common antigenic variant, followed by neural epidermal growth factor-like 1 protein-associated MN (NELL1-MN). Few studies have directly compared the outcomes of these two variants.AIMTo compare the outcomes of NELL1-MN with PLA2R-MN.

title: Lupus nephritis and kidney transplantation: A narrative review of patient and graft outcomes
creator: Tabassum Elahi, Saima Ahmed, Muhammed Mubarak
description: Lupus nephritis (LN), a serious manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus, continues to be a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Despite significant advances in immunosuppressive therapy, many patients progress to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), for which kidney transplantation (KT) remains the treatment of choice. However, the survival advantage of KT in LN-related ESKD is not yet clearly defined.

title: Predictors of one-year mortality in hemodialysis patients with end-stage renal disease at a Kenyan county hospital
creator: Felix Pius Omullo, Thomas Kimanzi Kitheghe, Maureen Mueni Mark, Allan Kariuki Ng’ang’a, Magdalene Wanjiru Parsimei, Wambugu Charles Kanyi, Ooko Anyang’o Emma, Ismail Abdi Sheikh, Joshua Macharia Gitumu, Abel Mwangi Gakuya, Glory Kawira Gitonga, John Alex Ndung’u, Elisheba Moraa Nyaro
description: BACKGROUNDIn Kenya, end-stage renal disease (ESRD) poses a significant public health burden. While hemodialysis is primarily delivered through county hospitals, comprehensive outcome data from these routine clinical settings remain scarce.AIMTo evaluate one-year clinical outcomes and identify independent predictors of mortality among ESRD patients undergoing hemodialysis at a Kenyan county hospital.

title: Identification of an isoflavone 6-hydroxylase involved in tectorigenin biosynthesis in kudzu (Pueraria montana var. lobata) and the efficient production of 6-methoxyisoflavones
creator: Kai Uchida, Masami Yokota Hirai
description: Kudzu (Pueraria montana var. lobata) produces several isoflavones that have beneficial effects in humans. These isoflavones accumulate in a tissue-specific manner, with 5,7,4′-trihydroxy-6-methoxyisoflavone (tectorigenin) and its derivatives accumulating mainly in flowers. Tectorigenin has various beneficial effects on humans and is in high demand, but its biosynthesis has not been elucidated, making large-scale production difficult.

title: Multiple forms of protein–protein and DNA binding are exhibited by BrxC from the BREX phage restriction system
creator: Alexander J Kaiser, Jennifer J Readshaw, Lindsey A Doyle, Maria Puiu, Abigail Kelly, Sydney F McGuire, Julieta Peralta Acosta, Duc Vu, Andrew Nelson, Darren L Smith, Lidia Araújo-Bazán, Ernesto Arias-Palomo, Yvette A Luyten, Barry L Stoddard, Tim R Blower, Brett K Kaiser
description: Bacteriophage exclusion (BREX) defense systems restrict phage infection via inhibition of phage DNA replication, while also modifying and protecting the bacterial genome. Type I BREX systems encode six conserved proteins, including a site-specific DNA methyltransferase. Host methylation requires a subset of BREX proteins, whereas phage restriction generally requires them all, suggesting that distinct but overlapping complexes mediate these activities.

title: Development of a Low-resource TELE-assisted Home Exercise Program for Balance and Functional Mobility in Parkinson’s Disease (TELEPORT-PD): An International e-Delphi Consensus
creator: Arnold Fredrick D’Souza, Manikandan Natarajan, Dushyanth Babu Jasti, Auwal Abdullahi, Mohammad Al-Wardat, Mohan Ganesan, Divyani Garg, Sudhir Prabhu Haladi, Pawan Raj Pulu Ishwara, Violaine Lavoie, Francesco Lena, Selva Ganapathy Velayutham, Susan L. Whitney
description: Despite the recent surge in the use of telerehabilitation (TR) for neurological disorders, there is a lack of TR programs tailored to persons with Parkinson’s disease (PwPD), particularly in low-resource settings. To address this gap, we aimed to develop a tele-assisted home exercise program for improving balance and functional mobility in PwPD (TELEPORT-PD).

title: Reversible Rapidly Progressive Dementia Due to Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
creator: Godknows Osarhiaekhimen, Ayomide Ayo-Salami, Adeolu Morawo
description: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is a vascular disorder of the brain caused by beta-amyloid deposits in small- and medium-sized vessels. In some patients, the condition triggers an inflammatory response, which can appear in different forms based on the pattern of vessel involvement.

title: Association of Interleukin-4 (rs224320), Interleukin-18 (rs1946518 and rs187238), and Tumor Necrosis Factor Receptor 2 (rs1061622) Gene Polymorphisms With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in a Rural South-Western Maharashtra Population
creator: Monika S Patil, Priyanka M Mane, Shivani R Kale, Sonika S Patil, Satish V Kakade, Satish Patil
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic inflammatory-metabolic disorder in which cytokine-mediated pathways play a crucial role in insulin resistance and β-cell dysfunction. Genetic polymorphisms in inflammatory cytokine genes such as interleukin-4 (IL-4) (rs224320), interleukin-18 (IL-18) (rs1946518 and rs187238), and tumor necrosis factor receptor 2 (TNFR2) (rs1061622) may influence individual risk of T2DM; however, region-specific data from south-western rural Maharashtra, India, remain limited.Objectives: The primary objective was to compare the genotype distributions of selected IL-4 (rs224320), IL-18 (rs1946518 and rs187238),

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Virtual Reality in Physical Rehabilitation: A Review of Machine-Learning Kinematics, Educational Scaffolding, and Treatment Adherence Strategies
creator: Magalli Diaz Bravo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Physical rehabilitation increasingly depends on interventions that are intensive, personalized, and sustained outside the clinic. Yet contemporary rehabilitation systems face persistent barriers, including workforce shortages, geographic inequities, rising costs, fragmented follow-up, and poor adherence to home exercise programs.

title: Long-Term Disease Control With Second-Line Nivolumab Monotherapy in Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma: A Case Report
creator: Shohei Otsuka, Kei Hiraoka, Nozomu Iwashiro
description: Nivolumab is recommended as second-line therapy for malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM); however, durable responses remain uncommon. In addition, combination immune checkpoint inhibitors are frequently limited by immune-related adverse events. A 72-year-old man with epithelioid MPM underwent extrapleural pneumonectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with cisplatin and pemetrexed. After recurrence, additional platinum-based chemotherapy was administered, followed by disease progression.

title: Bilateral Wrist Septic Arthritis Caused by Group B β-Hemolytic Streptococcus: A Case Report
creator: Adam C Dickerson, Mebeli Becerra, Chinmay Patel, Eric H Chou
description: Septic arthritis is typically a monoarticular infection most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus; however, polyarticular presentations are uncommon and associated with higher morbidity and mortality. Group B β-hemolytic Streptococcus is a less frequent pathogen but may occur in patients with significant comorbidities or recent obstetric events.

title: Mineral Bone Disorders in Chronic Kidney Disease Stages 3 and 4 With Special Reference to Bone Mineral Density Assessment Using Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DEXA) Scan: A Prospective Observational Study From Northeast India
creator: Prodip K Doley, Angelia L Khawbung, Manjuri Sharma, Gayatri Pegu, Miranda Pegu
description: BackgroundChronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD) is a systemic complication characterized by biochemical disturbances in calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone (PTH), and vitamin D metabolism. These abnormalities impair bone strength and promote vascular calcification, increasing fracture and cardiovascular risk. Early CKD stages (3 and 4) provide an opportunity for detection and intervention. Data on Indian pre-dialysis populations remain limited.

title: Improvements in Social Quality of Life for Recovering Addicts Receiving Dental Implant Rehabilitation
creator: Austin F Crossanoff, William L Balanoff
description: Substance use disorders (SUDs) are associated with severe oral deterioration, chronic systemic inflammation, and elevated depression risk, yet definitive dental rehabilitation is rarely integrated into long-term recovery care. This IRB-approved retrospective cohort study evaluated the effect of full-arch implant rehabilitation on depressive symptoms in 101 consecutively treated adults with verified long-term recovery from SUDs.

title: Use of advanced cardiovascular imaging in rheumatic immune-mediated inflammatory diseases
creator: Leher Gumber, Mohammed Askari Meghji, Vishal Kakkar, Karthikeyan Sivasankaran, Zahra M Iftikhar, Najla Elndari, Charlotte Talbot, Jason M Tarkin, Sven Plein, Marc R Dweck, Taryn Youngstein, Ziad Mallat, Lesley-Anne Bissell, Jonathan Heaney, John Reynolds, Maya H Buch
description: ObjectivesTo evaluate the real-world use of advanced cardiovascular imaging in less common and rare rheumatic immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) and identify variation in practice to inform future studies and clinical guidelines.MethodsA retrospective, multicentre quality improvement project was conducted across four major hospitals in the UK.

title: First population-based national eHealth system study on the prevalence of nonmalignant thyroid disorders in North Macedonia: A cross-sectional analysis
creator: Ana Talevska, Ivica Smokovski, Zhaklina Chagoroska, Emilija Antova, Lisa Zottarelli, Colton Daniels, Larisa Ozeryansky, Thankam Sunil
description: ObjectiveThyroid disorders are among the most common endocrine conditions worldwide. However, in the Republic of North Macedonia, national level data on their prevalence and demographic distribution are lacking. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and demographic patterns of nonmalignant thyroid disorders using data from the National eHealth System.

title: Failure rates of 958 interradicular mini-screws for maxillary total arch distalization following a well-established insertion protocol
creator: Lara Bettenhäuser-Hartung, Frauke Beyling, Rainer Schwestka-Polly, Christos Katsaros, Jonas Q Schmid
description: ObjectivesMaxillary Total Arch Distalization (MTAD) with interradicular mini-screws (MSs) in combination with Completely Customized Lingual Appliances (CCLAs) is an effective concept for Class II correction in adolescents and adults which does not require any additional supraconstructions. The aim of this study was to investigate the failure rates of MSs after strictly following a defined insertion protocol.

title: General practice care models and satisfaction in Australian residential aged care homes: a national survey of GPs, practice nurses, and managers
creator: Kate H Marshall, Mary A Burns, Christopher J Poulos, Roslyn G Poulos, Andrew Montague, Ebony T Lewis, Russell Pearson, Joel J Rhee
description: BackgroundResidential aged care homes (RACHs) in Australia support a growing population with complex healthcare needs. General practitioners (GPs), supported by practice nurses (PNs) and practice managers (PMs), play a central role providing medical care. Care models vary widely in these settings, and evidence on provider satisfaction and workforce sustainability is fragmented.

title: Adverse Childhood Events, not age of Acquiring Smartphones or Tablets, Predict Mental Health in Young Adults
creator: Christopher J. Ferguson
description: Objectiverecent years have seen considerable attention to concerns regarding youth access to screens. Many professional bodies and clinicians have advised parents to limit youth access to smartphones and tablets, particularly at young ages. However, little clear evidence has emerged to support this advice.Methoda dataset of 80,878 young adults (mean age: 23.3) was provided by Sapienlabs.

title: Determinants of Health-Related Quality of Life Among Patients with Psoriasis Vulgaris
creator: Bui Long, Nguyen Thi Kim Huong, Le Huu Doanh, Nguyen Hoang Long
description: Objectivepsoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated disease that significantly impacts patients' health-related quality of life (HRQOL). While effective treatments exist, the burden of psoriasis on HRQOL and the factors influencing it remain underexplored in Vietnam. To assess HRQOL and its associated factors among patients with psoriasis vulgaris in a tertiary hospital in Vietnam.

title: Effect of antihypertensive medication reduction on short-term blood pressure control in older adults: calibration of OPTiMISE trial results to real-world primary care data
creator: Antoine Christiaens, Ariel Wang, David A McAllister, Richard J McManus, James P Sheppard
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWhile antihypertensive treatment prevents cardiovascular events, it may also increase risks such as falls in patients with frailty. The Optimising Treatment for Mild Systolic Hypertension in the Elderly (OPTiMISE) trial found that deprescribing one antihypertensive drug did not result in worse short-term blood pressure control and long-term follow-up showed no observed harm, but its generalisability to routine clinical practice remains uncertain.ObjectiveThis study aimed to calibrate the OPTiMISE effect to a representative primary care population in England.MethodsWe calibrated the OPTiMISE treatment effect using

title: Applicability Evaluation Guideline for Diagnostic Criteria of Chinese Medicine Syndromes
creator: Jiansheng Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimTo develop a guideline for the applicability evaluation tool of the Diagnostic Criteria for Chinese Medicine Syndromes, aiming to enhance the clinical applicability of syndrome diagnostic criteria and promote their widespread adoption and application.MethodsThis guideline was developed using the Delphi method, with reference to the Guideline on Establishing Diagnostic Criteria of Chinese Medicine Syndromes, relevant international evaluation tools, and published diagnostic criteria for Chinese medicine syndromes.ResultsThe guideline specifies the principles, procedures, and scoring criteria for evaluating the applicability of traditional Chinese medicine

title: Compliance to direct oral anticoagulation therapy and clinical outcomes after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: a nationwide cohort study
creator: Bjarke Sihm Stender, Victor Kjær Eskildsen, Anders Kramer, Maja Hellfritzsch Poulsen, Kasper Korsholm, Kasper Bonnesen, Morten Schmidt, Mads Brix Kronborg, Jens Erik Nielsen-Kudsk
description: Background and aimsLife-long direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) therapy is recommended after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) in high-risk patients (CHA2DS2-VA≥2). Long-term DOAC compliance is crucial for effective stroke prevention. This study seeks to evaluate long-term compliance measured by adherence and persistence to DOAC therapy following first-time catheter abltation for AF.

title: Diversidad genética y resistencia antirretroviral del virus de la inmunodeficiencia humana de tipo 1 en personal militar peruano a los 12 y a los 18 meses de seguimiento
creator: Jonathan Guerrero, Dilan Suárez, Carlos Augusto Yabar
description: ResumenIntroducción. Se desconocen los factores que afectan la diversidad genética y las mutaciones de resistencia al tratamiento antirretroviral del virus de la inmunodeficiencia humana en personal militar.Objetivo. Describir los factores que afectan la variabilidad genética y la resistencia a los antirretrovirales del virus de la inmunodeficiencia humana en población militar durante un año de seguimiento.Materiales y métodos.

title: La salud mental en Colombia, ¿es un derecho o un privilegio?
creator: Martha Escobar, Álvaro Arenas, Camilo Perdomo-Luna, Darío Londoño, Juan Carlos Molano, María Nieto, Elizabeth Borrero, Esteban Vanegas
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ResumenEste artículo ofrece una visión de la situación de la salud mental en Colombia, destacando su creciente relevancia en la esfera pública y los desafíos específicos que enfrenta el país al respecto. Asimismo, analiza el impacto del conflicto armado y la pandemia de la COVID-19 en la salud mental de la población colombiana, subrayando cómo estas situaciones han exacerbado los problemas preexistentes.

title: Enfermedades huérfanas o raras en Colombia: situación actual y sugerencias para un futuro mejor
creator: Luis Alejandro Barrera
description: a menos de 1 individuo por cada 2000. Según esta definición que se usa en la mayor parte del mundo, existen entre 7000 y 10 000 enfermedades raras 1. En Colombia, se clasifican como «raras» a las que afectan a menos de 1 individuo por cada 5000 y, actualmente, se aceptan como tales a 2273 enfermedades.

title: Barriers to Nutrition Security in the US
creator: Caroline E. Owens, Ronit Ridberg, Julia Reedy Sharib, Hope C. Craig, Dariush Mozaffarian
description: This cross-sectional study of US adults assesses associations among barriers to healthy eating, sociodemographic characteristics, and health conditions driven by poor diet. Introduction Poor nutrition is a leading driver of morbidity and mortality, accounting for an estimated 45% of cardiovascular disease mortality, 70% of new diabetes cases, and $1.

title: Bypassing mandibular osseous defect using the high oblique sagittal split osteotomy: a case report and review of literature
creator: Sung Jun Ma, Gary James Chern-Wei Teoh, Leonardo Saigo
description: The presence of a mandibular osseous defect significantly complicates revision orthognathic surgery by increasing the risk of unfavorable fractures and inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) injury. In such instances, the high oblique sagittal split osteotomy (HOSSO) serves as a strategic alternative to the conventional bilateral sagittal split osteotomy.

title: Discovering the abstruse: reverse marginal mandibulectomy
creator: Rajendra Toprani, Padminii Ellapakurthi, Ashay Shah, Ramanarayana Boyapati, Aditya Mohan Alwala
description: Tumours involving the bones of maxillofacial region requires elaborate surgical skills and experience for managing the complexity. Treatment planning majorly depends on the extent of bone involvement, type of erosion and involvement of para mandibular soft tissue. Pertaining to mandible in this paper, marginal and segmental mandibulectomies are the predominant options which are oncologically safe practices done by surgeons.

title: Gas–Lesion Contact and Postural Compliance After Vitrectomy With Tamponade: A Continuous Monitoring and 3D Quantitative Analysis
creator: Hyunmin Na, Changhoon Baek, Seung Woo Choi, Eun Kyoung Lee, Un Chul Park, Kyu Hyung Park, Saram Lee, Chang Ki Yoon
description: PurposeTo assess postoperative head positioning behavior and estimate gas–retinal lesion contact after vitrectomy using a wearable accelerometer-based monitoring system and geometric modeling.MethodsThis study enrolled 56 patients who underwent pars plana vitrectomy between November 2024 and June 2025. Of these, 28 were prescribed prone positioning for 1 week and 28 received no postural instruction.

title: VeloRM: disentangling pre- and post-splicing RNA modification dynamics at single-cell resolution
creator: Haozhe Wang, Bowen Song, Zhixing Wu, Yigan Zhang, Jiayi Li, Yuxin Zhang, Anh Nguyen, Jionglong Su, Daniel J Rigden, Yijun Tang, Guifang Jia, Jia Meng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). RNA modifications critically regulate RNA function and fate, yet their dynamic changes across the RNA life cycle and during cellular transitions remain largely unexplored. Here we introduce VeloRM, a computational framework that captures RNA modification dynamics at single-cell resolution. VeloRM uniquely disentangles presplicing and postsplicing epitranscriptomes, enabling for the first time the identification and differentiation of modification sites on transcripts before versus after splicing.

title: Designing Integrated Virtual Care Partnerships: Insights from a Practice-Based Case Series at Mayo Clinic
creator: Lindsey M. Philpot, Margaret A. McIntee, Elton A. Mosman, John M. Davis, Megan Dulohery Scrodin, Brian M. Dougan, Stephanie L. Hansel, Xiao Jing Wang, Ziad Zoghby, Jon O. Ebbert
description: Access to high-quality primary and specialty care remains a persistent challenge in the United States, with millions of individuals facing barriers due to geography, provider shortages, and health inequities. As health care systems seek innovative solutions, virtual care providers have emerged as critical partners in expanding access, enhancing continuity, and supporting transitions across the health care continuum.

title: Emerging resistance in staphylococci following long-term dalbavancin treatment for prosthetic joint infections
creator: Ronja Hugg, Marc Stegger, Bo Söderquist
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and objectivesDalbavancin, a lipoglycopeptide with a half-life of 150–200 h, is a promising treatment option for prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) and other orthopaedic implant-associated infections (IAIs) caused by multidrug-resistant staphylococci. However, in vitro studies have shown that when exposed to low concentrations of dalbavancin, staphylococcal strains resistant to dalbavancin can emerge, potentially affecting its effectiveness in cases of recurrent infection.

title: Screening for Missed Opportunities for Diagnosis in the ED Using eTriggers and Large Language Models
creator: Clifford M. Marks, Sean Gibney, Bryan Stenson, Deesha Sarma, Cynthia Gaudet, Haadi Mombini, Thomas A. Buckley, Mario Keko, Larry A. Nathanson, Laura G. Burke, Nathan I. Shapiro, Jonathan L. Burstein, Shamai A. Grossman, Anika Parab, Alexander T. Janke, Arjun K. Manrai, Richard A. Taylor, Carlo L. Ro
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This diagnostic study compares the ability of 6 different large language models (LLMs) to identify missed opportunities for diagnosis among patients admitted to emergency departments (EDs) that use electronic trigger (eTrigger) tools for quality and safety surveillance.

title: Life’s Essential 8 in Pregnancy and Time to Incident Cardiometabolic Disease Over 7 Years Follow-Up
creator: Ellen C. Francis, Shalin Patel, Anushka Pande, Alexa Freedman, Lauren Keenan-Devlin, Linda M. Ernst, Emily S. Barrett, Ann Borders, Gregory E. Miller, Shristi Rawal, Amy H. Crockett
description: Key PointsQuestionIs cardiovascular health during pregnancy, assessed using a modified Life’s Essential 8 score (mLE8), associated with time to incident cardiometabolic disease after pregnancy?FindingsIn this cohort study of 1225 pregnancies, healthier mLE8 scores were associated with a significantly longer time to diagnosis of chronic hypertension and metabolic conditions.

title: Deep-ZOMA: A Deep Learning-Based Approach for Automated Morphometric Analysis of Zebrafish Larvae Ocular Structures
creator: Youyuan Zhuang, Chuang Xu, Wei Dai, Dandan Li, Xinyan Jiang, Huaiyuan Ding, Yuhe Yang, Ruowen Qiu, Zhen Ji Chen, Jiyuan Fang, Hui Yang, Jian Yuan, Jia Qu, Jianzhong Su
description: PurposeZebrafish (Danio rerio) ocular measurements are widely used in ocular disease research and drug discovery. Traditional methods rely on manual annotations, causing challenges in precision, efficiency, and workload. Here, we introduce a deep learning-based zebrafish ocular morphometric analysis (Deep-ZOMA) tool for quantitative measurement of zebrafish larvae ocular structures.

title: Vonoprazan in erosive esophagitis: Influence of gender and hiatus hernia on outcomes
creator: Muhammad Shoaib Khan, Mohammad Iltaf, Naeem Jan, Adnan ur Rehman
description: Objective:This study aimed to determine the efficacy of vonoprazan in erosive esophagitis and association of gender and hiatus hernia with treatment outcomes.Methodology:This prospective single arm cohort study (before and after treatment) was conducted from 1st January to 31st August 2025 in Department of Gastroenterology, HMC Peshawar. Non-probability convenience sampling technique was used.

title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Undergraduate Medical Student Assessment, Scientific Writing & Peer Review: Promise, Pitfalls, and the Need for Educational Governance
creator: Kamran Sattar, Mohamad-Hani Temsah, Shaukat Ali Jawaid
description: on. GenAI is now being explored for item writing, MCQ flaw detection, feedback generation, reflective writing assessment, short-answer grading, clinical reasoning support, and academic analytics. For undergraduate medical education, assessment is one of the most sensitive areas for AI integration because assessment decisions directly influence student progression, professional identity formation, patient safety, and public trust.

title: Emotional Intelligence and Academic Performance among Male and Female Medical Undergraduates in rural Sindh province, Pakistan
creator: Seema Bibi Qureshi, Ambreen Usmani, Junaid Tariq
description: Background & Objectives:Medical undergraduates face demanding requirements that heighten risk of stress, burnout, and poor performance. Emotional intelligence (EI), the ability to perceive, understand, and manage emotions supports resilience, well-being, and learning. However, evidence from Pakistan is inconsistent, with existing studies generally reporting moderate EI levels and context-dependent associations with academic outcomes.

title: Early targeted next-generation sequencing accelerates clinical recovery in children with community-acquired pneumonia: A retrospective study
creator: Di Lian, Dong Wang, Chenye Lin, QiuYu Tang
description: Background & Objective:The clinical impact of testing timing for targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) in pediatric community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is poorly understood. We hypothesized that early tNGS implementation accelerates clinical recovery and evaluated its comprehensive value.Methodology:In a retrospective study at Fujian Children’s Hospital (2021-2023), 199 hospitalized children with CAP (BALF tested) were analyzed. Patients were grouped by tNGS vs.

title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of the Structural and Thermodynamic Properties of Poly( l ‑lactic acid) in the Presence of Water
creator: Kalle Tuomi, Terttu I. Hukka, Jurkka Kuusipalo, Mikko Karttunen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In this study, we used all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the behavior of poly­( l -lactic acid) (PLLA) in the presence of 0, 1, 2, 6, and 12 m-% water. We focus on understanding how the contacts between various atoms of adjacent PLLA chains evolve and how these changes influence the system’s volume, density, and mechanical and thermodynamic properties.

title: The Efficacy of Acupuncture and Bee Venom Injections in Improving Hearing in a Patient with Idiopathic Conductive Hearing Loss: a case report
creator: Eun Kyung Lee, Min Hee Kim
description: Conductive hearing loss (CHL) is commonly caused by tympanic membrane perforation or otitis media. Congenital ossicular anomalies and otosclerosis are the primary considerations in patients with normal tympanic membranes and external auditory canals, whereas stapedius tendon abnormalities are less frequently observed.

title: Tracheal nebulization of AAV-CRE for lung conditional knockout model construction and whole lung clearing
creator: Lihong Ye, Xiyue Yan, Dacheng Yang, Shuang Wu, Wandong Chen, Wei Kevin Zhang
description: The development of lung-specific conditional knockout animal models is pivotal in advancing lung disease research. This protocol describes the experimental procedures in detail, including the construction of loxP mice, endotracheal tube nebulization of adeno-associated virus (AAV) and whole lung clearing. Mouse lung conditional knockouts were successfully constructed.

title: Detection of mutant cancer-derived circRNAs in extracellular vesicles by rolling circle amplification
creator: Mikołaj Piotr Zaborowski, Charles Pin-Kuang Lai, Alessandro Sammarco, Bence György, Xuan Zhang, Kyungheon Lee, Young Jeong Na, Lorenzo Ceppi, Koen Breyne, Elizabeth Marie Champagne, Jack Cardini, Robert Alexander Wesselhoeft, Marcin Iwanicki, Ralph Weissleder, Michael J. Birrer, Hakho Lee, Bakhos A.
description: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) form during splicing as a closed ring and are more resistant to degradation than linear RNAs. Cells release circRNAs within membrane-bound extracellular vesicles (EVs), which transport DNA, RNA, and proteins. Whether circRNAs in EVs can be used as biomarkers remains uncertain. We aimed to identify mutant circRNAs in EVs to develop a new biomarker approach.

title: Hybrid Governance: Negotiating justice for health services in informal urban settlements in Dhaka, Bangladesh
creator: Bachera Aktar, Kim Ozano, Sabina Faiz Rashid, Linda Waldman, Sally Theobald
description: This paper examines the complex governance landscape of public health service delivery in the informal urban settlements of Dhaka, Bangladesh, through the application of Hybrid Governance and Urban Political Ecology (UPE) frameworks. Rapid urbanization and insufficient state capacity have led to the development of informal settlements, where conventional governance structures are absent.

title: Can innovation strengthen resilient, just and sustainable health systems in disaster-prone settings? Insights from HSR2024
creator: Nanuka Jalaghonia, Rumana Huque, David Daniels
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Health systems in disaster-prone settings face recurrent shocks that expose and often deepen existing inequities. Increasingly, innovation, particularly digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI), is positioned as a pathway to strengthen resilience, responsiveness, and accountability. Drawing on insights from innovation-focused sessions at the 8th Global Symposium on Health Systems Research, this commentary examines whether and under what conditions innovation can contribute to resilient, just and sustainable health systems.

title: Author Correction: TGF-β promotes pericyte–myofibroblast transition in subretinal fibrosis through the Smad2/3 and Akt/mTOR pathways

title: Do Artifacts From Dental Implants Impair the Diagnosis of Simulated Internal Root Resorption in Cone‐Beam CT?
creator: Matheus Sampaio‐Oliveira, Fernanda Bulhões Fagundes, Luiz Eduardo Marinho‐Vieira, Rubens Spin‐Neto, Matheus L Oliveira
description: ObjectivesTo evaluate the influence of artifacts generated by dental implants on the diagnosis of simulated internal root resorption (IRR) in cone‐beam computed tomography (CBCT), considering implant number and composition.Materials and MethodsThirty‐five single‐rooted teeth were allocated into two groups: with simulated IRR (n = 15) and without IRR (n = 20). IRR was simulated using 37% hydrochloric acid for 3 h.

title: Flower‐rich and diverse road verges support pollinators, but traffic speed limits the ecological benefits across Europe
creator: Chris Wyver, Andrijana Andrić, Carolin Biegerl, Sofia Blomqvist, Christophe Dominik, Noah Feldmann, William Fiordaliso, Mike Garratt, Andrea Holzschuh, Hanna Honchar, Reet Karise, Maja Knežević, Hanno Korten, Sarah Lescot, Egle Liiskmann, John MacArthur, Marika Mänd, Denis Michez, Erik Öckinger, Oli
description: Roads are vital for human societies, yet they can also have negative impacts on the ecological communities that live in close proximity to them. Insect pollinators, which nest and forage in road verges running alongside roads, are a group of particular importance.

title: Xiasangju Processing Residues Improve Production Performance and Modulate Intestinal Inflammation and Gut Microbiota in Laying Hens
creator: Yiwei Jin, Lu Liu, Wei Wang, Pingping Li, Panpan Shi, Wei Liu, Peng Huang
description: Simple SummaryXiasangju processing residues are plant-based by-products generated during the production of traditional Chinese medicine formulations, which may still contain polyphenols, flavonoids, and certain nutrients. This study evaluated the potential effects of incorporating this processingby-products into the diets of laying hens during the late laying period.

title: From Resistance to Redesign—The Emerging Logic of Hybrid Care in Treatment-Resistant Depression
creator: Federico Mucci, Riccardo Gurrieri, Siham Bouanani, Matteo Gambini, Gerardo Russomanno, Donatella Marazziti
description: Highlights What are the main findings? The TRD trial landscape is dominated by device-based neuromodulation (48.1%) and pharmacological strategies with novel mechanisms (36.3%); biologic/novel agents (6.8%) and digital–hybrid programs (2.1%) form smaller strata.Trials are predominantly mid-phase with small-to-moderate sample sizes and heterogeneous endpoints, although 63.3% adopt standard clinician-rated scales. What are the implications of the main findings?

title: Clinical and radiological outcomes of balloon kyphoplasty: lateral decubitus versus prone positioning: a retrospective comparative study
creator: Ali Murat Başak, Ali Aydilek, Ömer Levent Karadamar, Bariş Çakmak, Erkan Sabri Ertaş, Mustafa Aydin, Tolga Ege
description: Osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures are common in the elderly, leading to pain, disability, and reduced quality of life. Balloon kyphoplasty (BK) is a minimally invasive treatment for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures, typically performed in the prone position. However, the prone position is not suitable for patients with severe comorbidities, such as morbid obesity.

title: Analysis of clinical characteristics of 38 patients with dextrocardia: An observational study
creator: Yongguang Li, Chong Wang, Xiaokai Li, Yu Fan, Biao Zhang, Chengzhen Rong, Susu Li, Zihan Sun
description: Dextrocardia is an extremely rare congenital anomaly, and survival into adulthood is exceptionally uncommon. This study aimed to systematically analyze the clinical, imaging, laboratory, and functional characteristics of patients with Dextrocardia to improve understanding of its natural history and prognosis. A retrospective review of 38 patients diagnosed with Dextrocardia at a single center from 2012 to 2025 was conducted.

title: Albumin-corrected anion gap and mortality risk in cardiorenal syndrome: Insights from a nationally representative cohort study
creator: Hongman Li, Xing Huang, Shengyong Si, Zhijing Li, Chun Zhao, Xue Zhao, Mengdie Liu, Yuan Deng, Xue Zhao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The prognostic significance of the albumin-corrected anion gap (ACAG) in patients with cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between ACAG and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in a nationally representative cohort. We identified 1783 patients with CRS from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005 to 2018 cycles and categorized them into terciles based on ACAG levels.

title: Research on RARs in neurodegenerative diseases: A bibliometric analysis
creator: Ting Wu, Tengyu Zhang, Ahmad Khaled Harb, Xiaojie Zhai, Wei Cui, Yunfei Cao, Xiang Wu
description: Background:In recent decades, thousands of research articles on neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) have been published. Retinoic acid and its analogues play crucial roles in biological processes such as cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis through their interaction with retinoic acid receptors (RARs).

title: Assessing the role of vitamins in dental caries occurrence: A retrospective study using NHANES data 2011 to 2018
creator: Jingna Huang, Ye Zhang, Bo Zeng
description: This study aims to investigate the relationship between vitamin intake and the occurrence of dental caries. This study was a retrospective study that collected data from the National Health And Nutrition Examination Survey database from 2011 to 2018. The number of dental caries teeth was determined using the Radike AW.

title: Medical students’ knowledge and attitudes towards integrative care with traditional Chinese medicine in Taiwan during the COVID-19 pandemic
creator: Sunny Jui-Shan Lin, Shung-Tai Ho, Yi-Chang Su, Chien-Sung Tsai, Shu-Meng Cheng, Cheng-Yi Cheng, Chien-Jung Lin, Tso-Chou Lin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In 2020, a novel botanical preparation of traditional Chinese medicine was developed and officially recommended for treating mild COVID-19 cases in Taiwan. This study examined the perceptions of integrative care combining Western and Chinese medicine in Taiwanese medical students. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted in April and May 2020 among first- to fourth-year medical undergraduates to evaluate their knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors regarding the use of Chinese medicine in integrative health care.

title: Effects of a home-based exercise and physical activity intervention after inpatient rehabilitation on real-world mobility in older adults with cognitive impairment: a secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial
creator: Christian Werner, Phoebe Ullrich, Letizia Degli Angeli, Rieke Trumpf, Tim Fleiner, Jose L Albites-Sanabria, Luca Palmerini, Bastian Abel, Martin Bongartz, Tobias Eckert, Jürgen M Bauer, Klaus Hauer
description: BackgroundPersistent mobility limitations after inpatient rehabilitation are common in older adults with cognitive impairment (CI). Home-based exercise interventions can improve locomotor capacity during this vulnerable period; however, evidence that they improve real-world mobility is scarce.ObjectiveTo investigate the effects of a home-based exercise programme combined with physical activity (PA) promotion on real-world digital mobility outcomes (DMOs).DesignSingle-centre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.SettingCommunity.

title: Procedure time and 90-day outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy for large-core stroke
creator: Chengsong Yue, Shihai Yang, Rongzong Li, Linyu Li, Jie Yang, Xiaolei Shi, Wenjie Zi, Yi Lin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionProcedure time during endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) has been associated with outcomes in general thrombectomy cohorts, but whether this relationship reflects a threshold or continuous risk accumulation in large-core stroke remains unclear.Patients and methodsWe performed a retrospective observational analysis of 490 patients with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion (LVO) and large-core infarction, defined by an Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score of 5 or less, from a prospective multicentre registry across 38 centres. Procedure time was analysed categorically and continuously.

title: GLP-1 Prescriptions for Weight Loss by Differences in Insurance Plan Coverage
creator: Mahnum Shahzad, Protima Advani, Oluwayomi Akintola, Michael Chernew
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This cross-sectional study reports trends in glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) prescriptions for plans that do and do not cover GLP-1s for weight loss. Introduction Coverage of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) drugs for weight loss is controversial.

title: Gaze behavior during closed-captioned movie viewing adapts to absent audio through more frequent switching between text and scene
creator: Anna Behler, Megan E. J. Campbell, Brodi Bathgate, Chanelle Noble, Johan van der Meer, Saurabh Sonkusare, Michael Breakspear
description: Closed captions, originally for hearing-impaired audiences, are now increasingly used, adding an additional visual element to the multisensory experience of movie viewing. This study examines how gaze behavior adapts to the absence of auditory information by testing whether increased caption engagement reflects more frequent switching between closed captions and the visual scene, longer uninterrupted reading intervals, or both.

title: Correction to: Feasibility and acceptability of an unsupervised and adapted physical activity program (PACE tool) as pragmatic care in a geriatric outpatient clinic
creator: Unknown

title: Layered Double Hydroxide-Stabilized AgI Photocatalyst for Efficient Arene Arylation and Alkylation
creator: Pengfei Han, Eric R. Waclawik, Steven E. Bottle, Qi Xiao, Xuheng Yang, Cheng-an Tao, Jianfang Wang, Huai Yong Zhu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Developing clean and efficient methods for carbon–carbon bond formation remains a central challenge in sustainable chemistry. Here, we report a unified photocatalytic strategy for direct arene arylation and alkylation under visible light. By integrating silver iodide (AgI) nanoparticles with magnesium–aluminum-layered double hydroxide (Mg2Al1-LDH), we achieve efficient cross-coupling of arenes with both aryl and unactivated alkyl iodides under mild conditions and natural sunlight.

title: Respiratory symptoms and exercise responses among adult E‐cigarette users with and without obesity
creator: Joseph W Walsh, Michael Beck, Alice Hinton, Theodore L Wagener, Jason E Lang, Jing G Wang, Dharini M Bhammar
description: Despite the high prevalence of both e‐cigarette use and obesity among young adults, little is known about whether obesity worsens lung function, ventilatory constraints, or respiratory symptoms among e‐cigarette users. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of obesity on lung function, ventilatory constraints, and exertional breathlessness in young adult e‐cigarette users.

title: Rapid Evolution of Ionic Silver Resistance in Escherichia Phage T7
creator: Larisa Chila Kiki, Monela Ntonifor, Walter LaDelle, Ugonna Morikwe, Franklin Ezeanowai, Lindsey McGee, Akamu Ewunkem, Joseph Graves, Liesl Jeffers-Francis
description: The antimicrobial resistance crisis has led to the use of metals and bacteriophages as possible alternatives to antibiotics. Experimental studies have examined interactions between ionic/nano-silver and bacteriophages against multidrug-resistant bacteria. However, these approaches have often failed to examine whether silver affects the stability and infectivity of bacteriophages.

title: Kidney Function-Specific Performance of High-Sensitivity Troponin T and I Using 0/1 h and 0/3 h Protocols in Suspected Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome
creator: Krongkarn Sutham, Boriboon Chenthanakij, Aumarin Kumpool, Theerapon Tangsuwanaruk, Arintaya Phrommintikul, Borwon Wittayachamnankul, Rudklao Sairai, Wachira Wongtanasarasin
description: Background/Objectives: Impaired kidney function is associated with persistently elevated cardiac troponin levels, complicating evaluation of suspected non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). The comparative performance of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) and I (hs-cTnI) across sampling intervals in this population remains uncertain.

title: Association of armed conflict and global measles cases: A structural equation modeling analysis of 193 countries from 2000 to 2023
creator: Tyler Y. Headley, Yesim Tozan, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha
description: BackgroundGlobal armed conflict and population displacement are increasing, yet their association with population health remains poorly understood. We developed and tested four theoretical models linking armed conflict, population displacement, and socioeconomic development to measles burden across 193 countries from 2000 to 2023.

title: Control Subarea Division for Coordinated Signal Control: A Colored Random Walk and Path Entropy Approach to Traffic-State Propagation
creator: Pengcheng Li, Bin Li, Lin Wang, Wei Zhang, Sixian Li, Jun Hua
description: Control subarea division is essential for coordinated signal control, but methods based mainly on local correlation or static topology may not adequately capture traffic-state propagation under dynamic traffic loading. This study proposes a control subarea division method that explicitly models traffic-state propagation by integrating state-guided colored random walk and path entropy analysis.

title: Entropy Gap as a Measure of Epistemic Caution in Credal Sets Generated from Data
creator: María Isabel A. Benítez, Carlos J. Mantas, Joaquín Abellán
description: Imprecise probability models generated from data represent epistemic uncertainty by replacing the precise empirical distribution with a set of compatible probability distributions. When this set is described by reachable probability intervals, the induced bounds are tight, so the represented imprecision is not inflated by unattainable interval limits.

title: Modeling and Simulation of Mass Transfer in Food Processing: Recent Advances in Governing Equations, Workflow, and Applications
creator: Sihui Chen, Zhou Qin, Tianxing Wang, Junjun Zhang, Roujia Zhang, Yucheng Zou, Jiyong Shi
description: Mass transfer is central to food processing but remains difficult to quantify because food materials are heterogeneous, multiphase, porous, biologically structured, and dynamically changing. Under these conditions, experiments alone cannot fully capture the spatiotemporal complexity of transport behavior, making modeling and simulation essential for mechanism interpretation, process prediction, and engineering optimization.

title: Prophylactic Use of Tranexamic Acid to Prevent Postpartum Hemorrhage in High-Risk Cesarean Deliveries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
creator: Xochitl Sandoval López, Hazel C. García, Cesar M. Gavidia, Karina V. Alam, Zaida I. Álvarez, Mirna E. Meléndez, David A. Tejada
description: Background/Objective: Postpartum hemorrhage is a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly among high-risk women undergoing cesarean section. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of prophylactic tranexamic acid in high-risk cesarean sections. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2.

title: Reviewing the Computational Landscape of Drug Repurposing: Evolution from Structure-Based Methods to LLM-Based Methods
creator: Zengyun Mou, Zhiqing Tian, Jiaqi Jin, Heng Yu, Yongzhen Huang
description: Traditional drug discovery is a high-risk, time-consuming, and costly endeavor. Drug repurposing has emerged as a pivotal strategy to overcome these challenges by identifying new therapeutic indications for approved drugs, thereby significantly reducing development timelines, costs, and safety risks. This review aims to provide a comprehensive methodological survey of computational strategies for drug repurposing.

title: Non-invasive assessment of the ventricular arrhythmogenic substrate beyond scar in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: NIAVAS-2 study
creator: J Reventos-Presmanes, E Guillen, E Ayauja, E Arbelo, E Guasch, J M Tolosana, L Mont, A M Guillem, A M Climent, A Porta-Sanchez, I Roca-Luque
description: BackgroundVentricular tachycardias (VTs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM), yet accurate risk stratification remains a clinical challenge. Fibrosis in NICM is often mid-wall or patchy and frequently adjacent or dissociated from regions of slow conduction or re-entry, making substrate localization based on imaging particularly challenging.

title: Correction: Kurhaluk et al. Role of Antioxidants in Modulating the Microbiota–Gut–Brain Axis and Their Impact on Neurodegenerative Diseases. Int. J. Mol. Sci. 2025, 26, 3658
creator: Natalia Kurhaluk, Piotr Kamiński, Rafał Bilski, Renata Kołodziejska, Alina Woźniak, Halina Tkaczenko

title: Kilovoltage Energy Significantly Enhances the Therapeutic Efficacy of Low-Dose Radiation in a 3xTg-AD Mouse Model of Alzheimer’s Disease
creator: Seungwon Lee, Ye Jin Yoo, Gyehyeong Kim, Eunsu Kim, Subin Yun, Joon Kim, Hoon Ryu, Weonkuu Chung
description: Low-dose radiation (LDR) has emerged as a promising therapeutic modality for Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). Although different irradiation protocols have been explored, the optimal parameters for maximizing therapeutic efficacy remain unclear. Radiation energy has been shown to influence radiobiological responses, with more pronounced effects at lower energy ranges.

title: Procedural Optimization in CT-Guided Lung Biopsy: Impact of Needle Angle and Patient Positioning on Complication Rates
creator: Erkan Bilgin, Ahmet Bayrak, Çetin İmamoğlu, Ezel Yaltırık Bilgin, Almıla Coşkun Bilge, Elif Aktaş, Hüseyin Çakmak, Banu İnce Alkan
description: Background/Objectives: CT-guided lung biopsy is an essential diagnostic procedure but is associated with complications such as pneumothorax and pulmonary hemorrhage. While patient- and lesion-related factors are well established, operator-modifiable parameters remain less clearly defined. This study aimed to evaluate complication rates and identify independent predictors, with a particular focus on modifiable procedural factors.

title: Long-term outcomes of catheter ablation for sustained ventricular tachycardia in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
creator: A Keresteci, C Coteli, H Yorgun, K Aytemir
description: BackgroundHypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetic myocardial disease associated with ventricular arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death (SCD). Although implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) have reduced the incidence of SCD, many patients with HCM continue to experience frequent shocks due to monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT), particularly in the presence of apical aneurysms or end-stage (dilated-phase) remodeling.

title: Artificial intelligence-powered ECG is superior to NT-proBNP in predicting left ventricular systolic dysfunction in atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
creator: O Baqal, C Yee, J Quillen, X C Mee, G K Lim, C Ayoub, R Arsanjani, D Sorajja, P Noseworthy, H El Masry
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionDespite its prevalence, risk stratification for tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy remains poorly understood. title: A Novel Swarm Intelligence-Driven Feature Selection for Interpretable Machine Learning in Multiparametric MRI-Based GBM Overall Survival Analysis
creator: Abdulkerim Duman, Xianfang Sun, James R. Powell, Emiliano Spezi
description: Simple SummaryThis study developed and validated an interpretable machine learning (ML) model using a novel swarm intelligence (SI)-based feature selection method with multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived radiomic features (RFs) to estimate overall survival (OS) in patients with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM).

title: From the Cochlea to the Cortex: Toward Integrated Auditory Health—Editorial for the Special Issue “Recent Advances in Hearing Impairment”
creator: Agnieszka J. Szczepek
description: area depends on coordinated efforts across multiple levels: from understanding molecular mechanisms at the synapse, through clinical diagnosis and treatments, to the cortical networks responsible for perception and consciousness. This Special Issue, “Recent Advances in Hearing Impairment,” compiles eleven contributions that follow the auditory pathway: from the periphery to the cortex.

title: Marshall-plan ablation strategy for recurrent persistent atrial fibrillation in patients with durably isolated pulmonary veins
creator: F Akerstrom, E Charitakis, A Paul-Nordin, S Saygi, E Svennberg, F Braunschweig, M Jensen-Urstad, N Drca
description: BackgroundThere is evidence that vein of Marshall (VoM) ethanol infusion, as part of a standardized lesion set (Marshall-plan) in persistent atrial fibrillation (AF), reduces atrial arrhythmia recurrence when compared to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) alone. However, data on the effectiveness of the Marshall-plan in repeat procedures with durable PVI is scarce.

title: Footwear Heel Height and Gait Biomechanics in Healthy Young Women: A Within-Subject Analysis of Spatiotemporal Parameters, Propulsion, and Pelvic Kinematics
creator: Alina-Daniela Totorean, Oana Cristina Radulescu, Alexandra-Magdalena Ioana, Laura Maghiar, Andreea Nita, Andreea-Adriana Neamțu, Elena Amaricai, Roxana Ramona Onofrei, Oana Suciu, Cristina Dumitrescu, Dan Iliescu, Florin Huț
description: Background: High-heeled footwear is widely used by women, yet its systemic influence on spatiotemporal gait parameters, pelvic kinematics, and propulsion across a range of heel heights remains incompletely characterised. This study aimed to quantify gait changes across four footwear conditions and assess the contribution of anthropometric characteristics to observed gait variability.

title: Current Status and Challenges of Local Resection for Early Gastric Cancer in East Asia
creator: Shinichi Kinami, Yasuto Tomita, Koichi Okamoto, Hiroyuki Takamura
description: Simple SummaryStandard gastrectomy with lymph node dissection for early gastric cancer typically achieves good oncologic control; however, post-gastrectomy syndromes and long-term nutritional impairment may ensue. In early gastric cancer, the risk of nodal metastasis is relatively low, suggesting that local resection may be feasible for carefully selected patients. Sentinel node biopsy can facilitate the intraoperative diagnosis of node-negative cases.

title: Establishment of In Ovo Salmonella Enteritidis Infection and Synbiotic Delivery Models in Chick Embryos and Their Effects on Early Gut Health
creator: Riliang Liu, Jiguang Wang, Jiying Dai, Yamei Wang, Weijiang Zheng, Wen Yao
description: Simple SummaryEarly life is critical for gut development and microbial colonization in chicks. However, it remains unclear how harmful or beneficial microbial exposure during embryonic development affects intestinal health after hatching. In this model-establishment study, we preliminarily established an in ovo Salmonella Enteritidis infection model and an in ovo synbiotic delivery model in chicks.

title: Tailoring Oncofertility to Breast Cancer Subtype: A Systematic Review of Fertility Preservation Strategies in Premenopausal Women
creator: Maryam Garba Oloriegbe, Olena Bolgova, Rasha Alissa, Aliaa Abdelmeguid, Hamida Garba Oloriegbe, Umaiza Rehan, Volodymyr Mavrych
description: Simple Summary Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women worldwide, and its diagnosis in young women of reproductive age is increasingly frequent. Modern treatments have dramatically improved survival, but many of these therapies damage the ovaries and threaten future fertility, which can be profoundly distressing for young survivors.

title: Evaluating the use of drones within medical logistics: A patient-focused qualitative evaluation
creator: Colin B. Shore, Ashley Shepherd, Frances Hines, Hazel Dempsey, Karen Bell, Dylan Powell
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Drone technologies offer significant promise for enhancing medical logistics, particularly in rural and remote areas. However, despite several pilot trials across the UK, there remains a lack of evidence regarding patient perceptions of drone integration in routine healthcare delivery. This study aimed to explore patient perspectives on the use of drones in medical logistics, with a focus on cost, safety, and impact on quality of life amongst three medical areas (chemotherapy, lab diagnostics and blood products).

title: Charges, Reimbursement, and Healthcare Resource Utilization in Patients with Extremity Arterial Injury in the United States: Analysis of Linked Hospital Chargemaster and Claims Data
creator: Elizabeth Brouwer, Fulton Velez, Junwei Tan
description: Highlights What are the main findings? Infections, amputations, fractures, and post-discharge complications increased costs both before and after discharge.Patients treated with autologous vein grafts had fewer outpatient visits, emergency room visits, and hospitalizations than patients treated with other types of grafts. creator: Zainab R. Abdelrahman, Amani A. Harb, Shtaywy S. Abdalla
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Astragalus membranaceus, a medicinal plant used in traditional Chinese medicine for centuries, has attracted growing scientific attention for its potential anti-aging and anticancer properties, particularly for skin and bone health. Its key bioactive compounds like astragalosides, cycloastragenol, and its commercial derivative TA-65, have been associated with telomerase activation and telomere maintenance, suggesting a possible role in modulating cellular senescence and tissue repair processes. title: Sex differences after atrial fibrillation ablation: a patient level meta-analysis
creator: L Barbosa, A Rivera, V M R Oliveira, R L Miranda, B Araujo, J R G Costa, L Tartuce, C Pisani, M I Scanavacca, F Darrieux, J Brugada, B R Nascimento, M C P Nunes, R Mehran
description: BackgroundSeveral studies suggest a higher likelihood of atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after catheter ablation (CA) in women than in men, implying sex may be an independent risk factor. However, the magnitude and time-course of this sex effect remain unclear.PurposeTo quantify the time-dependent absolute and relative risk of AF recurrence in women compared with men following CA.

title: Not All Sleep Loss Is Equal: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Rodent Models, Their Neurobiological Validity, and Translational Relevance to Neurological Disease
creator: Edem Ekpenyong Edem, Sabiu Bala Soja, Mohammed Rabiu Abba, Kelechi Favour Chinyere, Linus Anderson Enye
description: Not all sleep loss is equal, and overlooking this limits progress in sleep and neurological disease research. We compared nine rodent sleep deprivation paradigms, gentle handling, multiple platform variants, disk-over-water, the Unpredictable Chronic Sleep Deprivation (UCSD) paradigm, novel object introduction, curling prevention by water, automated systems, and head-lifting, evaluating stress confounds, sleep stage specificity, chronicity, and neurobiological outcomes.

title: Application of Sensory Evaluation to Understand Fresh Apple Cultivar Acceptance in Kazakhstan
creator: Aidana Mashrapova, Bibinur Nurmanova, Zhuldyz Omarova, Alua Zeinulla, Didier Talamona, Mei Yen Chan
description: Cultivar portfolio decisions and postharvest quality management in Kazakhstani fresh apple markets are made without locally validated consumer sensory benchmarks, limiting producers’ and breeders’ ability to align product design with regional consumer expectations. This exploratory study develops and pilot-tests a consumer sensory evaluation framework for fresh apple cultivars among young adults in an urban Kazakhstani context.

title: Long-term electrical performance of leadless pacemakers in dialysis patients: a single-center cohort study

description: IntroductionLeadless pacemakers represent a major advancement in cardiac pacing, particularly for patients in whom traditional transvenous systems pose higher procedural and long-term risks. Individuals with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on dialysis are especially vulnerable due to limited vascular access, central venous stenosis, and increased infection risk.

description: Background/Objectives: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common supraventricular arrhythmia and one of the most commonly encountered heart conditions in clinical practice. Emerging evidence suggests a significant role of inflammation, endothelial disfunction and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling in the pathogenesis of AF.

title: Beyond the panacea: addressing the systemic failure in midlife female sexual health
creator: Mariam Sherif, Panayoti Bachkangi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Menopause is a universal midlife transition that profoundly impacts physical, psychological, and sexual wellbeing. In recent years, clinical and public attention has increasingly focused on post-reproductive health, with hormone replacement therapy and targeted symptom management gaining renewed prominence. While a growing array of evidence-based treatment options now exists to address vasomotor, mood, and sexual health concerns, the rapid expansion of therapeutic availability has introduced new clinical challenges.

title: Acute Onset of Suicidal Ideation after Starting Lemborexant in a Patient with a Mood Disorder
creator: Renato Rodrigo Silva, Marjorie Mastellaro Baruzzi, Bianca Besteti Fernandes Damiano, Rodolfo Furlan Damiano
description: A 24-year-old woman with treatment-resistant depressive symptoms and chronic insomnia developed acute, intrusive suicidal ideation with intent on day 5 after starting lemborexant 10 mg nightly. Emergency assessment did not identify intoxication, metabolic disturbance, psychosis, mania, akathisia, or other acute precipitants. Pretreatment polysomnography showed severe insomnia with a sleep efficiency of 14.5% and absent REM sleep, without sleep-disordered breathing.

title: High‐Energy Topological Edge States and Strain‐Induced Multiple Flat Bands in a Honeycomb Lattice
creator: Xiaoqin Bai, Haozhen Tian, Boris A Malomed, Rongcao Yang, Xiaojun Jia
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We propose a novel anti‐twig edge in the honeycomb lattice (HCL) that supports two symmetric high‐energy edge states. It is different from the twig edge supporting the zero‐energy flat band. Moreover, multiple flat bands are produced by applying a strain to the HCL with a twig edge or an anti‐twig edge, and the suppression or enhancement of the high‐energy edge state is observed.

title: Infrared‐Microwave Compatible Stealth Transparent Metasurface With Digital Camouflage and Hybrid Absorption‐Scattering
creator: Dan Liu, Yanzhao Wang, Kefeng Ji, Huanhuan Gao, Sihong Zhou, Tong Liu, He‐Xiu Xu
description: With the rapid advancement of detection technologies, single‐band stealth strategies have become ineffective, rendering research into multispectral compatible stealth imperative. Thus, there is a pressing need for stealth solutions enabling effective simultaneous stealth performance across visible, infrared (IR) and microwave bands.

title: 以尿崩症起病累及垂体柄的罕见Rosai-Dorfman病1例
creator: Lusha LI, Honghui HE, Shaoli ZHAO, Ling CHU, Ping JIN, 敏宁 彭
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rosai-Dorfman病(Rosai-Dorfman disease，RDD)是一类罕见的非朗格汉斯细胞组织细胞增生症。2024年8月中南大学湘雅三医院内分泌科收治1例38岁男性，以尿崩症为首发症状，病情迁延15年，逐渐进展为全垂体功能减退症。影像学提示垂体柄明显增粗、2处硬脑膜瘤样结节、多发骨质破坏、少许间质性肺炎及泌尿系统受累。经垂体柄活体组织检查后确诊为RDD，伴有BRAF V600E突变，予以BRAF抑制剂达拉非尼靶向治疗和垂体激素替代治疗。治疗8个月后复查头部磁共振，提示垂体柄增粗较前好转，2处硬脑膜瘤样结节消失，且患者生活质量明显改善。对本病例进行回顾性分析，可帮助临床医师对垂体柄增粗进行病因诊断及鉴别诊断，提高对RDD这一罕见疾病的认识。Keywords: Rosai-Dorfman病, 尿崩症, 垂体柄增粗, 多系统受累, BRAF突变

临床上中枢性尿崩症和垂体柄增粗可同时出现或先后出现，其病因诊断复杂且困难。很多患者在初次就诊时不一定能得到正确的诊断[1]。本研究报道1例以尿崩症为首发症状、病程长达15年的侵犯垂体柄、硬脑膜、骨骼等多系统的Rosai-Dorfman病(Rosai-Dorfman disease，RDD)患者，以提高内科医师对垂体柄增粗的诊断及鉴别诊断的能力，并认识这一疾病。

病例资料

患者，男，38岁，因“口干、多饮、多尿15年余，言语不利1个月余”于2024年8月2日入住中南大学湘雅三医院内分泌科(以下简称“我科”)。患者疾病自然史如图1所示。患者15年前无明显诱因出现口干、多饮、多尿，每日饮水3 000~4 000 mL，夜尿3~4次，曾在外院考虑“肾性尿崩症？”，出院后长期服用氢氯噻嗪和卡马西平，但疗效欠佳，遂于2013年3月14日第1次入住我科，禁水加压试验结果提示禁水后最高尿比重达1.020，尿渗透压616 mOsm/kg，垂体磁共振(magnetic resonance imaging，MRI)平扫及增强未见异常(图2A和2B)，诊断为“精神性烦渴”出院。出院后患者仍感口干多饮多尿，近年饮水量及尿量均为6 000~7 000 mL，夜间需起床上厕所及饮水3~4次。半年前患者自觉体力下降，性欲减退，体毛脱落，体重减轻约15 kg。入院前1个月无明显诱因出现言语不利，主要表现为吐词欠清，无头痛和视力下降，在外院MRI检查提示鞍区占位，为求进一步治疗遂第2次入我科。既往体健，否认传染病史，否认重大外伤、手术史。

title: 湖南省高校新生传染病认知的统计调查：HPV感染认知短板及其调节因素
creator: 李林 刘, 秀洪 袁
description: 目的高校新生是传染病健康教育的重要目标人群，提升其传染病防控知识水平对于促进校园公共卫生安全具有重要意义。了解湖南省高校新生对艾滋病(acquired immunodeficiency syndrome，AIDS)、人乳头瘤病毒(human papilloma virus，HPV)感染、乙型病毒性肝炎(以下简称“乙肝”)和肺结核(pulmonary tuberculosis，PTB)4种重要传染病的认知水平及其影响因素，重点探究学校层面特征(如学历结构、专业设置、地区)对学生传染病认知的差异化影响，为高校开展精准、有效的入学阶段健康教育提供实证依据。方法于2025年秋季学期，采用横断面调查方法，对湖南省36所高校(涵盖不同地区、层次和类型)的全体一年级新生进行匿名问卷调查。调查共回收有效问卷156 185份。问卷内容涵盖4种传染病的基础知识、传播途径及预防措施，并收集学校信息。以各题目回答正确率(比例数据)为因变量，经反正弦平方根变换后，构建线性混合效应模型进行分析。模型纳入学校所在地区、学校层次、是否设有临床医学专业、学生性别比例、本科学生比例、研究生比例及疾病类型等固定效应，并设置学校随机截距和题目随机截距(嵌套于疾病类型)以控制数据层次结构。通过比较包含交互项(重点关注本科比例、医学专业设置与疾病类型的交互)的模型与主效应模型，识别关键调节因素。结果新生对4种疾病相关知识的认知正确率总体分化显著：对AIDS(84.5%)与TB(90.6%)相关知识的认知正确率较高，而对HPV感染(55.1%)和乙肝(76.5%)相关知识的认知正确率较低，其中对HPV感染相关知识的认知正确率低于其他疾病(P<0.001)。本科比例呈现负向调节效应：学校本科学生比例对认知水平的影响因疾病类型而异；在控制其他变量后，本科比例对HPV感染和乙肝认知存在显著的负向调节作用(交互项均P<0.001)；即在本科比例较高的学校，新生对HPV感染和乙肝的认知相对于AIDS显著较低。医学专业发挥正向保护效应：学校设有临床医学专业对HPV感染认知存在显著的正向调节作用(P=0.024)；这表明，在医学专业院校，新生(包括非医学专业学生)的HPV感染相关知识的认知正确率显著优于非医学专业院校。其他因素影响有限：学校所在地区、学校层次及学生性别比例对总体相关知识的认知正确率无显著主效应或调节效应。研究生比例的影响未达到统计学意义。随机效应模型显示，学校间差异仅解释总变异的5.74%，而疾病间差异解释35.43%，表明认知差异主要源于疾病知识特性本身，高校间的教学影响在新生入学初期尚未成为主要分化来源。结论湖南省高校2025级新生对不同传染病的认知存在显著差异，其中对HPV感染相关知识的认知正确率最低。学校特征主要通过调节效应影响认知水平，本科比例较高的院校在HPV感染和乙肝认知方面相对存在劣势，而设有医学专业的高校与较高的HPV感染相关知识的认知正确率存在关联。高校新生入学阶段是开展针对性传染病健康教育的重要窗口期。高校环境因素对不同传染病认知水平的差异化调节作用，为传染病健康教育资源的精准配置提供了新的分析视角。 大学生群体作为国家未来发展的重要力量，其身心健康与社会稳定和进步息息相关。高校环境具有人口高度密集、集体生活接触频繁、人员跨地域流动性强等显著特征，这使得校园极易成为传染病传播与暴发的场所。具体而言，艾滋病(acquired immunodeficiency syndrome，AIDS)、人乳头瘤病毒(human papilloma virus，HPV)感染、乙型病毒性肝炎(以下简称“乙肝”)和肺结核(tuberculosis，TB)是当前威胁大学生群体健康的4种重点传染病。AIDS作为一种不可治愈的严重传染病，在青年学生中流行趋势严峻；HPV感染与多种癌症密切相关；病毒性肝炎可导致肝硬化、肝癌等严重后果；TB则具有高度传染性。然而，大学生群体对这些疾病的认知仍存在盲区：对传播途径存在误解(如误认为AIDS可通过日常接触传播)，对关键预防措施(如安全套使用、疫苗接种)的认知与践行不足，对疾病的隐匿性、主动检测的重要性及感染者的权益也缺乏清晰认识。这些认知不足不仅影响大学生对相关疾病风险的理解与防护，也使其在面对流感等传统传染病以及新型冠状病毒肺炎等新发传染病时面临更大的健康风险。因此，系统评估并提升大学生对传染病的认知水平、防控意识与健康相关行为能力，不仅是保障学生个体健康、维护正常教学秩序的必然要求，更是筑牢校园公共卫生安全防线、提升全社会突发公共卫生事件应对能力的战略基石[1-3]。 近年来，国内外学者围绕大学生传染病认知与防控开展了大量实证研究，普遍揭示了大学生群体传染病健康素养整体偏低的现状。大学生对传染病基本知识，如传播途径、核心症状、分类及疫苗原理等，知晓率不高，且存在显著差异。例如，师浩楠等[4]的研究发现，仅约55%的大学生会主动关注传染病常识，对甲类传染病包含种类的准确回答率不足一半。Delicati等[5]在意大利帕多瓦大学对1 059名不同专业的大学生开展了横断面调查，结果表明，医学生比非医学生对医源性感染的认知更高，个人照顾经历与新型冠状病毒肺炎疫情提升了学生对感染预防的重视，但知识差距依然存在，提示需将针对性预防教育纳入大学课程。Liou等[6-7]针对美国新泽西州立大学304名本科生的横断面调查显示，基于健康信念模型分析，女生比男生采取了更多预防新型冠状病毒肺炎感染的行为且健康信念的各维度得分更高，年长学生比年轻学生的预防行为更多且感知障碍更少，提示需针对不同群体设计干预措施以提升健康行为动机和自我效能。陈瑶等[8]在新发传染病疫情期间的调查中也指出，大学生对正确洗手、佩戴口罩等具体防护技能的知晓率仅为三至四成。这种认知短板直接影响了防护行为的依从性。研究进一步揭示了认知水平的影响因素具有多维度和不平衡性。人口学特征方面，普遍共识是女生的认知水平及行为依从性通常优于男生；医学专业学生因学科背景优势，其疾病相关的知识掌握程度、防护态度和行为实践均显著高于非医学专业学生；来自城镇、家庭社会经济地位较高(尤其母亲文化程度高)的学生往往表现出更好的健康素养。地域与环境因素亦发挥作用，如孙海峰等[9]发现济南高校农村生源学生的健康素养水平低于城市生源学生，少数民族学生低于汉族学生。此外，信息获取渠道高度依赖新媒体(如微信、微博)，但信息甄别能力不足可能带来误导风险[8]。 在干预层面，健康教育能有效提升大学生的“知信行”水平。通过健康知识科普讲座、互动教学、多媒体等多种形式结合的健康教育，能显著提升学生对传染病知识的掌握率和良好卫生习惯养成率。田鑫等[10]强调，提升“传染病健康素养”对促进正确预防行为(如咳嗽礼仪、公筷使用)具有关键作用。当前教育实践呼吁采用多元化、精准化的策略，如利用“互联网+”平台开展生动宣传、加强普及非医学生的医学常识、实施针对薄弱人群(如男生、农村生源、少数民族学生)的精准干预，并探索“医校联动”“同伴教育”等创新模式[4, 10]。国际上早已将健康素养视为个体乃至群体健康结局的核心决定因素之一，其在传染病预防控制领域的重要性在SARS、H1N1流感、埃博拉及新型冠状病毒感染等多次疫情中不断被验证和强化[11]。世界卫生组织(World Health Organization，WHO)等机构积极倡导将健康素养提升作为公共卫生干预的基础性战略。研究[12]表明，较高的健康素养能够帮助个体更好地理解疫情信息、遵从公共卫生建议、识别错误信息，从而采取有效的自我保护行为，并减轻疫情带来的心理恐慌。在国外的健康教育中，针对青年学生，尤其是大学生群体的研究，同样关注其健康素养水平及影响因素，并积极探索基于学校环境的健康促进项目。研究[13]不仅关注知识传播，更重视批判性思维培养、自我效能感提升及健康行为支持性环境的构建。这些理念与实践与国内研究倡导的“知信行”模式深化、精准化干预和多元化教育手段不谋而合，共同指向一个核心：提升以健康素养为基础的传染病综合防控能力。 综上所述，尽管国内外已有相当研究积累，但中国大学生传染病认知与防控仍面临认知基础不牢、群体差异显著、行为转化不足等挑战。湖南省作为中国的高等教育大省，拥有数量众多、类型各异的高校及庞大的在校大学生群体，这一密集且活跃的群体在校园内外构成了一个复杂而动态的公共卫生界面。然而，针对该区域大学生传染病认知水平与健康素养的系统性调查尚不充分，其认知现状、影响因素及群体内部差异(如西部和非西部高校、不同学历、不同性别)仍缺乏以本省数据为基础的精准画像。现有全国性研究虽揭示了普遍性问题，但难以直接指导具有湖南地方特色的校园健康教育实践。因此，在“健康中国”战略深入推进与后疫情时代校园常态化防控的背景下，立足于湖南省的实际情况，开展一项系统、深入的实证研究，全面评估本省大学生传染病认知与健康素养现状，并剖析其深层影响因素，对于填补地域研究空白、为省内教育及卫生部门制订精准化、差异化的校园健康促进与传染病防控干预策略，具有不可或缺的理论价值与现实紧迫性。 对象与方法 伦理声明 本研究已获得中南大学湘雅三医院医学伦理委员会批准(审批号：快26249)。 调查对象 本研究面向湖南省高等院校2025级入学新生，调查对象为湖南省36所高校2025级秋季学期首次进入当前培养阶段学习的新生群体，涵盖专科、本科及研究生不同培养层次的学生。参与高校涵盖综合类、医学类及职业院校等不同办学类型。 调查实施与质量控制 于2025年9月至10月采用方便整群抽样方法开展调查，调查主要在新生入学初期及系统性健康教育活动全面开展前实施，旨在尽可能反映学生入学阶段的基础传染病认知水平。本研究采用“问卷星”平台开展线上匿名问卷调查，由各高校统一组织实施，学生通过手机或电脑在线完成填写。调查过程中不收集姓名、学号等个人身份信息，以保障匿名性与数据真实性。为提高数据质量，问卷核心题项均设置为必答项，并对明显异常、信息不完整及答题时间过短的问卷进行筛除。问卷提交后由系统自动汇总，并在数据整理阶段进一步进行逻辑核查与数据清洗。 问卷描述 采用自编的《湖南省2025级新生传染性疾病相关知识调研问卷》进行横断面调查。问卷共分为5个部分：第1部分为一般人口学信息(就读学校、性别、就读阶段)；第2至5部分分别评估对AIDS、HPV感染、乙肝及TB共4种重点传染病的核心认知。问卷题型以单项选择题为主，在HPV感染与乙肝认知部分设置多选题，共计18个核心知识题项，上述4种传染病依次设8、4、2和4个。内容紧密围绕疾病的传播途径、关键预防措施(如安全套使用、疫苗接种)、常见误解澄清(如日常接触传播AIDS)、症状识别(如TB可疑症状)及正向态度(如主动检测、规范治疗、权益保护)等进行设计，旨在系统考察新生的知识认知准确度、误区辨识力及健康态度取向。 本问卷内容基于国家权威疾控机构发布的核心信息编制，主要用于高校新生传染病相关知识认知的现况调查。内容覆盖4种重点传染病的传播、预防及健康行为等方面，可用于初步评估高校新生相关传染病知识认知水平。本研究重点关注群体相关知识差异，因此未对问卷开展系统的测量信度和效度验证。 统计学处理 采用题目层面正确率作为认知指标。每道题目根据作答结果判定为“正确”或“错误/不知道”，认知正确率定义为某题目正确作答人数占该题目总作答人数的百分比。不同传染病的总体认知情况主要依据对应题目正确率的整体分布进行比较分析。统计方法采用单因素方差分析和t检验考察多组样本平均水平的差异；采用样本皮尔逊相关系数考察传染病和各变量之间的相关性；采用线性混合效应模型(linear mixed-effects model，LMM)分析高校新生传染病认知正确率的影响因素。由于传染病认知正确率 P 为比例数据(0~1之间)，在建模前对其进行反正弦平方根变换(arcsine square-root transformation，ASRT)，以符合模型的正态性和方差齐性假设。 模型构建 以个体的传染病认知正确率(ASRT后)为因变量。固定效应变量包括以下10个： 1)截距项：参照组为其他地区(Xi 1=0)、普通高校(Xi 2=0)、无临床医学类专业(Xi 3=0)、男生比例为0、本科比例为0、研究生比例为0的AIDS正确率。 2)考虑到湖南省高校地域、层次和专业分布的差异，为了考察这些差异对学生4种传染病认知能力的影响，本研究设置3个反应学校差异的变量：学校地域类型变量X 1(省会高校、西部高校和其他地区高校)；学校层次变量X 2(985/211/双一流高校和其他高校)、学校有无医学专业变量X 3(有临床医学专业和无临床医学专业)。变量X 1、X 2和X 3均为分类变量。对X 1的3个不同取值对应的正确率进行单因素方差分析，P<0.

title: 护士对基于AI动态评估静脉血栓栓塞风险接受度的潜在剖面分析及其影响因素
creator: 圣莉 程, 楠楠 李, 嘉 黄, 伟娜 王, 敏 方, 雪梅 詹, 文风 林, 凌云 田
description: 目的随着智慧护理的快速发展，用于动态评估静脉血栓栓塞(venous thromboembolism，VTE)风险的人工智能(artificial intelligence，AI)系统已在临床逐步推广，但护士作为该系统的直接应用者，其接受度的高低直接影响技术的临床应用效果。然而，护士对使用AI动态评估VTE风险的接受度是否存在群体异质性，目前尚不明确。本研究旨在通过潜在剖面分析(latent profile analysis，LPA)识别护士对使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度的潜在类别，并剖析其影响因素，为制订分群、分层的推广与培训方案提供实证依据。方法采用便利抽样法，于2025年4月至6月对安徽省皖南、皖中及皖北地区三级医院的护士进行调查，采用一般资料调查表、临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表、护士职业态度量表、护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度问卷进行调查。采用LPA识别护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度的潜在类别，多元Logistic回归分析探讨各因素对不同类别的影响。结果共回收有效问卷2 323份。护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度分为3个潜在剖面(3组)：低接受度-顾虑抗拒组[388例(16.8%)]；中接受度-谨慎观望组[1 177例(50.5%)]，高接受度-积极接纳组[758例(32.7%)]。护士工作年限、夜班频率、临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表中知识维度评分及护士职业态度量表评分是护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度潜在剖面的影响因素(均P<0.05)；在控制协变量后(以低接受度-顾虑抗拒组为参照)，护士职业态度量表评分越高，归入中接受度-谨慎观望组、高接受度-积极接纳组的可能性越大，比值比(odds ratio，OR)分别为1.023、1.074(均P<0.001)；夜班频率几乎很少甚至无与夜班频率为2~3次/月的护士更倾向归入中接受度-谨慎观望组(OR=1.773、OR=2.243，均P<0.05)与高接受度-积极接纳组(OR=3.964、OR=4.300，均P<0.001)；工作年限≤5年(OR=4.942，P<0.001)及10~19年(OR=3.361，P=0.006)的护士均更倾向于归入高接受度-积极接纳组；临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表中知识维度评分越高的护士，越易归入高接受度-积极接纳组(OR=1.042，P=0.009)。结论护士对基于AI动态评估VTE风险的接受度存在明显的群体异质性。医院管理者应重点关注对AI动态评估VTE风险接受度为“低接受度-顾虑抗拒”和“中接受度-谨慎观望”的护士，提升其对新技术的接受水平。 国家卫生健康委员会办公厅发布的《2025年国家医疗质量安全改进目标》[1]中“提高静脉血栓栓塞(venous thromboembolism，VTE)规范预防率”已连续5年成为国家医疗质量安全十大改进目标之一。VTE作为住院患者高发且可预防的致死性并发症，其早期精准风险评估是降低发病率的首要防线。目前临床VTE风险评估主要依赖人工评估量表[2-4]，其准确性高度依赖于护士的知识水平、临床经验甚至工作状态，存在评估效率偏低、漏判与误判风险较高等问题[5]。近年来，人工智能(artificial intelligence，AI)驱动的VTE动态风险评估系统已在临床广泛应用，有效提升了VTE风险预测的准确性与时效性[6-7]。尽管AI系统在VTE风险评估中展现出显著优势，但其在临床护理实践中的落地效果高度依赖于护士的接受度，即护士认同并主动采用该技术的主观意愿[8]。护士的接受度不仅直接影响AI系统的使用效能与工作流程优化，更决定了智慧护理技术能否真正转化为临床实效。然而，目前国内关于护士对AI动态评估VTE风险接受度的研究仍较为匮乏，且现有研究大多忽略了不同特质个体之间的差异，缺乏对群体异质性的深入探讨[9]。因此，本研究基于潜在剖面分析(latent profile analysis，LPA)[10]识别护士对使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度的潜在类别特征并深入剖析其影响因素，为医院护理管理者制订分群、分层的AI动态评估VTE风险推广与培训方案提供实证依据。 对象与方法 伦理声明 本研究已获得中国科学技术大学附属第一医院伦理委员会批准(审批号：2024KY伦审第485号)，调查对象均对本研究知情同意并自愿参与。 对象 2025年4月至6月，采用便利抽样法，选取安徽省皖南、皖中、皖北地区使用AI动态评估VTE风险的三级医院的2 500名护士为调查对象。纳入标准：1)年龄≥18岁；2)取得护士执业资格证书且工作时间≥1年；3)所在医院使用AI系统进行住院患者VTE风险动态评估的时间不少于3个月；4)近3个月内使用该系统的频率≥5次/周；5)对本研究知情同意，自愿参与。排除标准：1)调查期间不在岗(休假、外出学习等)；2)在院实习、规培、进修等。采用横断面研究样本量计算公式估算样本量，公式为n=(UαS/δ)2[11]，根据预实验(n=151)结果，S=2.318，取α=0.05，Uα =1.96，允许误差(δ)为0.12，同时考虑20%失访率，计算所需样本量为1 791例。 调查方法 一般资料调查表 研究者自行设计一般资料调查问卷，问卷包括性别、年龄、婚姻、人事关系、工作年限、护士层级、职称、工作职责、夜班频率，以及是否接受过AI动态评估VTE风险培训等。 护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度问卷 问卷由研究者以技术接受模型为理论框架自行编制。对11名VTE护理专家进行2轮函询，根据函询结果修订问卷内容。2轮专家函询中，有效问卷回收率均为100%，专家的权威系数为0.918，变异系数为0.115~0.327，肯德尔和谐系数分别为0.325、0.328(P<0.001)。最终形成的问卷包括4个维度、14个条目，分别为感知有用性维度(4个条目)、感知易用性维度(4个条目)、对AI信任度维度(3个条目)及使用意愿维度(3个条目)；采用Likert 5级计分法，每个条目从非常不同意至非常同意计分为1~5，总分为14~70，得分越高表示接受度越高。采用探索性因子分析检验问卷结构：Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin(KMO)值为0.924，Bartlett球形检验P<0.001，表明数据适合进行因子分析，累计方差贡献率为72.38%，各条目因子载荷为0.610~0.840，共同度范围为0.512~0.843，均大于0.500，表明各条目与所属公因子关系密切；采用验证性因子分析进一步检验量表的结构效度，基于修正指数并结合量表理论结构，对模型进行了适当修正。修正后模型的拟合结果显示：χ 2=119.656，自由度(df)=65，χ 2/df=1.841，比较拟合指数=0.971，拟合优度指数=0.900，近似误差均方根=0.075。综合各项拟合指标，模型与数据适配良好，符合结构方程模型拟合标准，表明量表具有良好的结构效度。本研究量表总体克龙巴赫α系数为0.865，各维度克龙巴赫α系数介于0.866至0.870之间，均达到0.700以上标准，提示量表整体及各维度条目内部一致性可靠。 临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表 临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表由杨梅等[12]编制，该量表包括知识、行为、态度3个维度共31个条目。采用Likert criterion，AIC)、贝叶斯信息准则(Bayesian information criterion，BIC)、样本校正的BIC(adjusted BIC，aBIC)，即3个指标数值越小代表模型拟合效果越好。2)分类评价指标：通过信息熵评估分类的精准性，取值为0~1，越接近1，表明分类精准性越高。3)似然比检验：通过罗-梦戴尔-鲁本校正似然比检验(Lo-Mendell-Rubin likelihood ratio test，LMRT)和基于Bootstrap的似然比检验(bootstrapped likelihood ratio test，BLRT)比较k个和k-1个类别模型间的拟合优度差异，当P<0.05时则前者最优[15]。本研究对各个模型结果进行综合判断，确定最佳模型。采用多元Logistic回归分析评估各因素对不同接受度类别的影响，检验水准α=0.05。 结 果 title: Perceived Healthcare Discrimination and Its Impact on Mistrust and Delayed Care Among Sexual and Gender Minority Young Adults in Spain
creator: Andrea Miranda-Tena, Francisco J. Sanmartín, Judith Velasco
description: Sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals face discrimination in health care, compromising both well-being and access to services. Such experiences may foster expectations of mistreatment and mistrust of health care professionals, contributing to delays in care with potentially adverse consequences.

title: Health effects associated with alcohol consumption: a Burden of Proof study
creator: Xiaochen Dai, Sneha I. Nicholson, Hilary R. Lawlor, Sinclair Carr, Jaimie D. Steinmetz, Natalie M. Chen, Susan A. McLaughlin, Simon I. Hay, Kanyin L. Ong, Aleksandr Y. Aravkin, Peng Zheng, Reed J. D. Sorensen, Nora M. Gilbertson, Erin C. Mullany, Erin M. O’Connell, Christopher J. L. Murray, Emmanuel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The relationship between alcohol and health is complex, and the evidence relating alcohol consumption to various cardiovascular diseases, cancers and other conditions is evolving. Moreover, alcohol drinking guidelines vary widely. Here we conducted 16 systematic reviews across four databases and conservatively re-evaluated dose–response relationships between alcohol consumption and 20 health outcomes, analysing 843 cohort and case–control studies using the Burden of Proof meta-analytic framework.

title: Advanced three-dimensional culture technologies in reproductive medicine: A narrative review
creator: Annahita Ghaedrahmati, Mohammad Zandi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Recent advancements in 3-dimensional (3D) in vitro culture systems for follicles, oocytes, and embryos represent a paradigm shift in assisted reproductive technologies and reproductive biology. By mimicking the native physiological microenvironment more faithfully than conventional 2-dimensional systems, these innovative platforms directly address critical limitations of current in vitro embryo production protocols, including low blastocyst development rates, compromised embryo quality, and concerning epigenetic aberrations.

title: Profiling arbutin as a potent cholinesterase and GSK-3β inhibitor and evaluating its cytotoxicity in SH-SY5Y cells for Alzheimer’s disease therapy
creator: Shirin TARBIAT, Tuğba BAL, Deniz GÜLMEZ
description: Background/aimAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder linked to cognitive decline and memory loss, marked by hyperphosphorylated tau tangles and decreased acetylcholine levels, which are affected by acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE) activity. Glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK-3β) also plays a role in AD through abnormal activation.

title: Study of Subclinical Hypothyroidism and its Association with Lipid Profile Among the Rural Population of Chamarajanagara District—A Hospital-Based Study
creator: B. V Sumanth, K. J Thoyaj, N Shashank
description: Background:Subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) patients are at an increased risk of coronary artery disease and cerebrovascular disease complications. The association between SCH and dyslipidemia is still controversial.Objectives:To study the prevalence of SCH in Chamarajanagara district and to find its association with lipid profile.Materials and Methods:A prospective cross-sectional study was carried out at Chamarajanagara Institute of Medical Sciences hospital, Chamarajanagar.

title: The Bacterial, Viral, and Microbiome Contributions in Cardiovascular Diseases: A Narrative Review
creator: Shyamala Ravikoti, Vikas Bhatia, Mohanasundari Saykkulandai Kuppuswamy
description: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While traditional risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes, and lifestyle behaviors are well-documented, emerging evidence highlights the role of microbial agents in contributing to cardiovascular risk. This narrative review explores the epidemiological evidence linking various microbes, including bacteria, viruses, and other pathogens, to cardiovascular diseases.

title: GPER介导的大气细颗粒物致肺癌作用研究进展
creator: Zhenhua LI, Dingbiao LI
